data_quality_notes: Paid spend is Meta Ads + Google Ads. GA4 contributes site revenue and traffic only, so spend is never double counted.
Platform revenue is each network's own attributed figure. Meta and Google both claim orders GA4 records once, so the two sides are shown separately rather than summed.
All ratios are computed from summed numerators and denominators across the range, not by averaging monthly ratios.

GA4 key events are the property's conversions metric, which counts every configured key event rather than purchases only. Average order value is therefore not derivable from this export; revenue per session is shown instead.
13.5% of GA4 sessions carry no source or medium, so channel-level traffic splits understate paid contribution.
GA4 revenue is analytics-attributed and may not match paid platform ROAS.
GA4 rows represent analytics session groupings, not ad platform entities.
Paid channel spend is sourced from Meta and Google Ads collector contracts.

flags.detail: 20/8/24 | GH | ABO | RTB was charged 5,084,411 in 2026-04 (18.6% of total paid spend) for 883,879 impressions and 77,416 clicks, with no conversions. That is a CPM of 5,752 against 75 for every other Meta campaign the same month — 77x the peer rate. The same delivery at peer rates would have cost about 66,423, leaving roughly 5,017,988 to query with the platform.
flags.title: Charge out of line with account rates

flags.detail: Meta holds 86% of paid spend and reports the higher platform ROAS, but GA4 credits it 2.48x against 6.19x for Google Ads. On analytics-attributed revenue Google Ads returns more per rupee.
flags.title: Budget concentrated in the lower-returning channel

flags.detail: Platform-reported ROAS fell from 15.6x in 2025-07 to 6.0x in 2026-06 (-61%).
flags.title: Google Ads ROAS decay

flags.detail: Platform-reported ROAS fell from 19.2x in 2025-07 to 12.3x in 2026-06 (-36%).
flags.title: Meta ROAS decay

flags.detail: GA4 could not identify a source for 34% of sessions in 2025-10, against 1% in 2026-06. 4 month(s) sit above 15%, so channel shares there are understated and trends spanning the break partly measure tracking rather than performance.
flags.title: Traffic attribution coverage changes mid-range

flags.detail: Meta and Google Ads together claim 2.80x the revenue GA4 recorded for the entire site. Treat platform ROAS as directional and judge budget on blended MER.
flags.title: Platform revenue exceeds analytics revenue

flags.detail: Active campaigns rose from 11 in 2025-07 to 30 in 2026-06 (2.7x) with no improvement in ROAS.
flags.title: Meta campaign count growing without efficiency gain

flags.detail: Active campaigns rose from 5 in 2025-07 to 10 in 2026-06 (2.0x) with no improvement in ROAS.
flags.title: Google Ads campaign count growing without efficiency gain
